title: Scurvy: vitamin C (water-soluble) deficiency causing ecchymoses
vignette: A 72-year-old man is brought to the hospital by paramedics after he was found disoriented and wandering in the street. He has a history of dementia, hypertension, and stroke. Physical examination reveals a disoriented, thin-appearing man. The gingivae are swollen and bleed easily, and ecchymoses are noted on the legs. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL (normal 13.5-17.5), platelets 152,000/mm3 (normal 150,000-400,000), white blood cell count 4,500/mm3 (normal 4,500-11,000), blood urea nitrogen 28 mg/dL, serum creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, prothrombin time (PT) 11 seconds (normal 11-15), and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) 30 seconds (normal 25-40). Which of the following is most likely responsible for this patient's ecchymoses?

clues.note: A thin, disoriented, likely poorly nourished elderly man is at risk for nutritional deficiencies - a clue to scurvy (vitamin C deficiency).

clues.text: gingivae are swollen and bleed easily
clues.note: Swollen, bleeding gums are a classic manifestation of scurvy, due to defective collagen weakening gingival vessels/connective tissue.

clues.text: ecchymoses are noted on the legs
clues.note: Easy bruising/ecchymoses reflect fragile perivascular collagen (poor vessel support) in vitamin C deficiency.
A normal platelet count (152,000 / normal 150,000-400,000) argues against thrombocytopenia/platelet dysfunction as the cause of bleeding.
Normal PT and PTT exclude coagulation-factor problems (e.g., vitamin K deficiency, liver disease), pointing to a vascular/collagen cause.

whatMatters: An undernourished elder with bleeding gums, easy bruising, anemia, but NORMAL platelets and NORMAL PT/PTT = scurvy (vitamin C deficiency). Vitamin C is a WATER-SOLUBLE vitamin required for collagen hydroxylation; its deficiency weakens perivascular collagen, causing fragile vessels and bleeding. Answer E (water-soluble vitamin deficiency).
strategy: Use the normal coagulation studies to localize the bleeding to a VASCULAR/collagen defect, then match the clinical picture (bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, poor wound healing, easy bruising) to vitamin C deficiency - a WATER-soluble vitamin. Reject fat-soluble vitamin K (prolongs PT), platelet dysfunction (normal count, but this is a collagen problem), hepatic dysfunction (would prolong PT), and zinc (perioral dermatitis, not gum bleeding).

eliminations.label: Endothelial cell dysfunction - von Willebrand pattern
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: endothelial/von Willebrand factor problems causing mucosal bleeding. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: von Willebrand disease typically prolongs PTT and is inherited; the clinical picture (bleeding gums, thin/undernourished elder) and normal PTT fit scurvy better. ✅ Correct if: mucocutaneous bleeding with prolonged PTT/abnormal vWF.

eliminations.label: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency - vitamin K (would prolong PT)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: vitamin K (a fat-soluble vitamin) deficiency impairs clotting factors II, VII, IX, X. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it would PROLONG the PT (and later PTT); this patient's PT/PTT are normal, so factor synthesis is intact. ✅ Correct if: easy bruising with a PROLONGED PT.

eliminations.label: Hepatic dysfunction - would prolong PT
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: liver failure reducing clotting-factor production. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it prolongs PT (and PTT); normal coagulation studies here exclude it. ✅ Correct if: coagulopathy with prolonged PT and stigmata of liver disease.

eliminations.label: Platelet dysfunction - count is normal, cause is collagen
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: qualitative/quantitative platelet problems causing mucocutaneous bleeding. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the platelet count is normal and the unifying findings (gum bleeding, perifollicular hemorrhage, poor healing) point to defective COLLAGEN, not platelets. ✅ Correct if: bleeding with thrombocytopenia or a platelet-function defect (e.g., uremia).

eliminations.label: Zinc deficiency - perioral dermatitis, not gum bleeding
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: zinc deficiency causing an erosive perioral/acral dermatitis, alopecia, and poor wound healing. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: gingival bleeding and easy bruising are not features of zinc deficiency. ✅ Correct if: perioral/acral rash + alopecia + impaired healing.

reasoning: Undernourished elder with bleeding gums + ecchymoses + anemia
Normal platelets and normal PT/PTT exclude platelet and coagulation-factor causes -> a vascular/collagen defect
Vitamin C (water-soluble) is required for collagen hydroxylation; deficiency causes fragile perivascular collagen = scurvy
mechanism: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a WATER-soluble vitamin that acts as a cofactor for prolyl and lysyl HYDROXYLASES in collagen synthesis, enabling the hydroxylation of proline/lysine that cross-links and stabilizes the collagen triple helix. In deficiency (scurvy) - seen with malnutrition, alcohol use disorder, or restrictive diets, as in this poorly nourished elderly man - defective collagen weakens the connective tissue supporting blood vessels, producing fragility and hemorrhage: swollen, bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhages with corkscrew hairs, easy bruising/ecchymoses, poor wound healing, and sometimes subperiosteal hemorrhage (arthralgia). Anemia is common (from bleeding and impaired iron absorption). Crucially, platelet count and coagulation studies (PT/PTT) are NORMAL, because the bleeding stems from a vascular/collagen defect, not a platelet or clotting-factor problem - the key discriminator here. Treatment is vitamin C repletion. Vitamin K (fat-soluble) deficiency and liver disease would prolong the PT, and zinc deficiency causes dermatitis, not gum bleeding.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biochem/Nutrition > vitamin C (water-soluble): cofactor for collagen prolyl/lysyl hydroxylase; scurvy = bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, poor healing, ecchymoses; normal platelets/PT/PTT.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Normal coagulation + platelet count localizes the bleeding to a collagen/vascular defect -> vitamin C (water-soluble).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on scurvy, ascorbic acid, prolyl hydroxylase, water- vs fat-soluble vitamins, or perifollicular hemorrhage? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Vitamin K (fat-soluble) and liver disease prolong PT; platelet count is normal; zinc = perioral dermatitis - only vitamin C fits.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: scurvy (vitamin C, water-soluble) -> defective collagen -> bleeding gums, ecchymoses, poor healing; normal PT/PTT/platelets.

memoryHook: No vitamin C, no collagen glue - vessels crumble, gums bleed, and bruises bloom, all while platelets and clotting times stay perfectly normal.
